name: ue-vscode-helper
displayName: Unreal Engine VS Code / Cursor Helper
description: Dual-host Unreal IntelliSense setup for VS Code (Microsoft C++) and Cursor (clangd + slim BuildRules IntelliSense), plus excludes and Git init

ue-vscode-helper.enginePath.description: Fallback path to your Unreal Engine installation when EngineAssociation cannot be resolved from the .uproject

ue-vscode-helper.preferHost.description: Which IntelliSense profile to apply. auto detects Cursor vs VS Code from the app name.

ue-vscode-helper.restoreModuleRules.description: On Cursor setup, run UE-bundled `dotnet restore` on the slim `.vscode/<Project>.BuildRules.IntelliSense.csproj` (wrapped by a sibling .sln as dotnet.defaultSolution — not the full Intermediate ModuleRules). Timeout 90s; non-fatal. Avoids indexing thousands of Engine Build.cs via UE5Rules.

ue-vscode-helper.ensureExtensions.description: During Setup, soft-prompt to install host-appropriate extensions before patching configs. required = IntelliSense core only; requiredAndOptional = full stack; off = skip. Never hard-fails Setup. Does not use package.json extensionDependencies.

ue-vscode-helper.promptPython.description: When ensureExtensions is not off, include a Python extension in the checklist (even on required mode). Cursor prefers anysphere.cursorpyright; either that or ms-python.python counts as satisfied. VS Code uses ms-python.python.
